rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed reading makes nasr worldly victory toward the goal and fath entry into Paradise, following the wording of 39:73.
rows.anchor: Üçüncü bir vecih: ‘Nusret’ dünyada maksûda zafer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearest interpretation is victory over Quraysh or the Arabs and the conquest of Mecca.
rows.anchor: ‘nasr’ın Kureyş’e veya bütün Arab’a galebe, ‘feth’in de Mekke fethi olmasıdır

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas's transmitted interpretation identifies the promised conquest as Mecca's conquest.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan menkul olan da Mekke’nin fethidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca's conquest is called the conquest of conquests; the Hudaybiyya treaty that preceded it was called a manifest conquest.
rows.anchor: ki ona “fethu’l-fütûh” yani “fetihlerin fethi” denilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The victory and Mecca's conquest opened later conquests and Islam's gates; construing nasr and fath generically points to the day of 5:3.
rows.anchor: birçok müfessirîn bu nasr u fethi cinse haml eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic reading is especially apt if the surah descended at Mina during the Farewell Pilgrimage, though the future sense then attaches to part of the vision.
rows.anchor: Haccetü’l-Vedâ‘da teşrik günlerinde Mina’da nâzil olduğu rivayetine göre bu mâna daha yakın olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fath means more than territorial conquest: Mecca and Taif's opening released hearts closed to truth into Islam in successive waves.
rows.anchor: “fetih”ten murad yalnız memleket fethinden ibaret olmayıp daha ziyade kalblerin iman ve İslâm’a fethi demek olur

rows.speaker: İsâm
rows.claim: Isam says the phrase about crowds entering suits the reading of fath as opening the religion's door to believers.
rows.anchor: Onun için İsâm demiştir ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca was conquered in Ramadan of year eight; the Prophet arrived with ten thousand and two thousand later joined, and he stayed fifteen days.
rows.anchor: Mekke’nin fethi hicretin sekizinci senesi ramazanında olmuştu, Resûlullah’ın maiyyetinde muhâcirîn ve ensar ve sâir mü’minlerden on bin kişilik muntazam bir ordu vardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Kaaba, the Prophet proclaimed God's oneness and victory, asked Meccans what they expected, then pardoned them as the released ones.
rows.anchor: onlara “tulekā” tâbir olundu

rows.speaker: Amr b. Seleme
rows.claim: Amr reports that tribes awaited Mecca's conquest, reasoning that if Muhammad prevailed over his people he was a prophet, then hastened to Islam.
rows.anchor: Buhârî Amr b. Seleme’den şöyle tahric eylemiştir

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: Hasan reports that Arabs reasoned one who defeated Mecca, once protected from the people of the Elephant, could not be overcome, so they entered in crowds.
rows.anchor: Hasan’dan da: “Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Mekke’yi fethedince

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority's Meccan conquest reading also means conquest of the Kaaba, opening Islam to hearts and humanity; worldly and spiritual expansion spread from its door.
rows.anchor: o yalnız âdî bir şehrin fethinden ibaret değil, Kâbe’nin fethi olduğundan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because wa-ra'ayta is coordinated with jaa, the whole idha clause forms one time and condition.
rows.anchor: Bâlâda söylendiği vechile bu “جَٓاءَ,”وَرَأَيْتَ’ye ma‘tuf olarak اِذَا mecmû‘unun başına dâhil bulunduğundan

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi takes the apparent scope of al-nas as all humanity beyond the Arabs.
rows.anchor: Râzî’nin dediği gibi “nâs”tan zâhir olan, Arab’ın gayriye de şâmil olmak üzere umum insanlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the wording first applies to Arabs, most exegetes specify Arabs; the intent is humanity beginning to enter collectively, not every individual.
rows.anchor: Onun için ekser müfessirîn Arab demişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human creation and reason aim at knowing and worshipping God; those who fail to know truth are likened to cattle or worse.
rows.anchor: insanlık hilkatinden ve akıldan maksud Allah’ı tanıyıp ibadet etmek olduğu cihetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ru'yet most naturally means seeing with the eyes, but may mean knowing as a cognition verb taking two objects.
rows.anchor: “Rü’yet”ten zâhir olan da gözle görmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ru'yet is ocular, people is the object and entering is their circumstantial state; if cognitive, people is the second object.
rows.anchor: “Rü’yet” basarî olduğuna göre “nâs” mef‘ûl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadkhulun rather than dakhalu shows entry has begun but is unfinished and continues successively, including future entrants.
rows.anchor: دَخَلُوا buyurulmayıp يَدْخُلُونَ buyurulması da hepsinin duhulleri tamam olmuş olmayıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah's religion is the true Islamic community; no other religion is accepted, as 3:19 and 3:85 state.
rows.anchor: Allah dinine yani hak islâm milletine ki Allah indinde din odur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who do not submit willingly will ultimately submit unwillingly and return to God.
rows.anchor: Allah’a tav‘an teslim olup da inkıyad etmeyen, nihâyet kerhen inkıyad etmeye mecbur olur

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Raghib defines fevc as a rapidly passing group, while allowing the broader sense of any group; both resemble an ala, or troop.
rows.anchor: Râgıb der ki: “‘Fevc’ sür‘atle geçen cemaattir”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural afwajan suggests groups arriving one after another, like a procession passing before the observer.
rows.anchor: “efvâcen” diye cemi‘lenmesi haysiyetiyle de fevcâ fevc, alay alay demek olacağından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This procession depicts the promised victory of the true religion over all religions, which began between Mecca's conquest and the Prophet's death.
rows.anchor: bu hak dinin bütün dinlere galebesinin zuhûru

rows.speaker: Ebû Ömer b. Abdülber
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr says no unbelievers remained in Arabia at the Prophet's death: after Mecca, Hunayn, and Taif, people entered individually or through delegations.
rows.anchor: Ebû Ömer b. Abdülber demiştir ki: “Resûlullah’ın vefatında Arab’da kâfir kalmamıştı

rows.speaker: İbn Atıyye
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya qualifies the report: no Arab idolaters remained, but Banu Taghlib Christians accepted jizya rather than Islam during the Prophet's life.
rows.anchor: İbn Atıyye de demiştir ki: “Bunun kâfir kalmamıştı demesinden murad Allahu a‘lem putperest Arab kalmamıştı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people meant are idolaters such as those of Mecca, Taif, Yemen, and Hawazin.
rows.anchor: O hâlde murad ehl-i Mekke, Tâif, Yemen

rows.speaker: İkrime ve Mukātil
rows.claim: A report from Ikrima and Muqatil identifies al-nas as Yemen's people, seven hundred of whom came as a delegation and accepted Islam.
rows.anchor: İkrime ve Mukātil’den bir rivayette de “nâs”tan murad ehl-i Yemen denilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A well-known hadith says faith and wisdom are Yemeni, linking the Yemenite delegation with these virtues.
rows.anchor: “iman Yemânî’dir, hikmet de Yemânî’dir, yani Yemen tarafına mensubdur”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Mecca, Hunayn, and the siege of Taif, delegations from all Arabia entered Islam over the next two years; Najran and Banu Taghlib accepted Islamic protection and allegiance, opening the call toward foreign states.
rows.anchor: Mekke’nin fethiyle akabindeki Huneyn muharebesi ve Tâif muhasarasından başka bir harb olmaksızın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These days fulfilled the promise of Islam's completion; the Prophet's mission and proclamation ended, with later duties entrusted to the community.
rows.anchor: Bununla Resûlullah’ın risalet ve tebliğ vazifesi hitâma ermiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the promised victory and mass entry, the Prophet should praise and glorify the Lord who nurtured and sent him, fulfilled His promise, granted Kawthar, and made his enemies abtar.
rows.anchor: artık tesbih et Rabbine hamd ile seni inayet ve terbiye-i hâssasıyla yetiştirip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wisdom and culmination of victory and spreading religion is glorification and praise; the people of Paradise and angels likewise praise God.
rows.anchor: nusret ve fetihten ve neşr-i dinden netice, gāye-i hikmet tesbih ve tahmiddir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All things glorify their Maker according to their own nature, so glorification with praise is the purpose of all creation.
rows.anchor: Ve hatta her şey kendi hususiyetine göre Hâlıkına hamd ile tesbih ettiğine nazaran

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih derives from swift swimming or passing and by extension means distancing or purifying; Raghib says it is hastening in worship and applies to speech, action, and intention, with prayer an inclusive reading of 37:143.
rows.anchor: “Tesbîh” esasen balığın suda, kuşun ve atın havada, nücûmun eflâkte hızla geçişleri gibi sür‘atle geçmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alhamdulillah and subhanallah are characteristic expressions of praise and glorification; tasbih can express admiration at beauty or disavowal of what is repugnant, and Subhan is also mentioned as a divine name.
rows.anchor: “Elhamdülillah” demek hamdin bir ifâde-i mahsûsası olduğu gibi, “sübhânallah” demek de tesbîhin bir alem-i mahsûsu

rows.speaker: Ebü’l-Bekā
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa says Quranic tasbih means prayer and also tanzih; with bi it signals prayer-coupled glorification, whereas tasbih negates what is unworthy and takdis affirms what befits God.
rows.anchor: Ebü’l-Bekā Külliyyât’ında da şöyle mezkurdur

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says tasbih denotes God's negative attributes of majesty and tahmid His positive attributes of beneficence, with negation preceding affirmation.
rows.anchor: Râzî der ki: “Hak teâlâ’nın sıfatları selb ü îcab, nefy ü isbatta mülâhaza olunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here bi does not govern tasbih; instead the command pairs glorification with praise.
rows.anchor: Yani burada bâ ile ta‘addî etmiş değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Combining tasbih and praise displays God's majesty and beneficence, corresponding to the name Dhu al-Jalal wa-al-Ikram.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde tesbih ile hamdin cem‘i Zü’l-celâli ve’l-ikrâm ismi hükmünce

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: The Prophet defines tasbih as declaring God free from every defect or blemish.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’e ‘tesbîh’ten sual olunduğunda buyurmuştur ki: تـَنْزِيهُ اللهِ مِنْ كُلِّ سُوءٍ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's transcendence covers His essence, attributes, acts, and names; it entails manifestation of majesty and the perfection of divine beauty.
rows.anchor: “tesbîh” Allah teâlâ’nın zâtında, sıfâtında, ef‘âlinde, esmâsında nezâhet ve paklığını ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thunder and angels' glorification makes tasbih's relation to divine majesty explicit.
rows.anchor: kavl-i ilâhîsi tesbîhin sıfât-ı celâl ile alâkasını açık olarak ifade etmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone performs tasbih and hamd in their full reality; created beings proclaim them according to innate gifts through deed, speech, and belief.
rows.anchor: Mahlûkāta ait olan tesbih ise her birinin mevâhib-i fıtriyesine göre mümkin olabilen istitâ‘at-i mahsûsası nisbetinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes understand tasbih here as tanzih, while some take it as prayer.
rows.anchor: ekser müfessirîn mutlaka tenzih ile, bazıları da namaz ile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes interpret tasbih as saying subhanallah, and others as astonished glorification of the victory's greatness.
rows.anchor: diğer bazıları da “sübhânallah” demek ile tefsir eylemişler

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Abu Suud summarizes the command as saying subhanallah with praise.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud bu vecihleri şöyle hulâsa eylemiştir: “Rabbine hamdederek ‘sübhânallah’ de

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Abu Suud also reads it as wonder at a victory and success beyond anyone's imagination.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud bu vecihleri şöyle hulâsa eylemiştir

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Abu Suud also interprets it as increased worship and praise in response to God's abundant favor.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud bu vecihleri şöyle hulâsa eylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Suud reads the command as prayer in gratitude for God's blessing; a report says the Prophet prayed eight forenoon rakas when the Kaaba was opened.
rows.anchor: Kâbe’nin kapısını açtığı zaman Resûlullah’ın sekiz rek‘at kuşluk namazı kılmış olduğu rivayet olunmuştur

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Abu Suud also reads it as praising God for fulfilling His promise while declaring Him free of what wrongdoers allege.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud bu vecihleri şöyle hulâsa eylemiştir

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Abu Suud's final gloss praises God's attributes of generosity and glorifies Him through His attributes of majesty.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud bu vecihleri şöyle hulâsa eylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Prophet had long been commanded to glorify and praise, this command carries a special nuance such as continuation or intensification; exegetes explain its occasion.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’ın birçok âyetlerde geçtiği üzere daha evvelden dahi tesbih ve hamd ile emrolunduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's majesty and beneficence manifest continuously, so praise is always due and can mean gratitude for bestowed blessings as well as other gifts.
rows.anchor: her zaman O’na tesbih ve hamd vazifedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As divine majesty and generosity increase, glorification and praise must increase; forgetting God amid blessings is ignorance and ingratitude.
rows.anchor: asıl bu muvaffakiyeti müşahededen sonra tesbih ve hamdin ziyadesiyle îfâsı maksuddur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After success the heart should turn to God with greater inward purity, as 94:7–8 commands; Paradise likewise culminates in glorification and praise.
rows.anchor: kalbin daha yüksek bir ferağ ve temizlikle Hak teâlâ’nın celâl ve cemâli neş’esini duyarak O’na müteveccih olması lâzımdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance expresses longing for God; breaking idols and erasing visible and inward traces of polytheism fulfill the command's purifying force.
rows.anchor: zâhir ü bâtında şirk âsâr ve ahlâk ve âdâtının silinmesi için tathîrât icrâsı da o tesbih ve tenzîhin muktezâsıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No creature can fully glorify or praise God, even if sinless, because creaturely imperfection is intrinsic and all excellence depends on God's aid.
rows.anchor: dünyada hiçbir mahlûkun O’nu bütün kemâliyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet says he cannot exhaustively praise God, who is as He has praised Himself; a further transmitted saying admits worship never fulfills God's due.
rows.anchor: لاَ أُحْصِي ثـَنَاءً عَلَيْكَ أَنْتَ كَمَا أَثـْنـَيْتَ عَلَى نـَفْسِكَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God's forgiveness can cover human deficiency, so the command to seek forgiveness points to the promised mercy of the Lord.
rows.anchor: Bu kusuru örtecek, bu eksikliği ikmal edecek olan da ancak Allah teâlâ’nın mağfiretidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to seek forgiveness applies to the Prophet and his community, perhaps even more to the community, as 47:19 and 48:2 indicate.
rows.anchor: gerek kendin ve gerek ümmetin için mağfiretini dile

rows.speaker: İbn Receb
rows.claim: Ibn Rajab says bare istighfar joined with a request for pardon includes repentance, while explicitly adding tawba makes istighfar a simple prayer for pardon.
rows.anchor: İbn Receb demiştir ki: “Mücerred istiğfar, duada mağfiret talebiyle beraber tevbedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Rajab defines repentant istighfar as regret for past sin and resolve against future sin; the saying about persistence and seeking pardon refers to this form.
rows.anchor: Bir de demiştir ki: “Mücerred istiğfar geçmiş günaha nedâmetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legally promised effects attach to istighfar understood as repentance; pardon-seeking without regret is merely prayer and poor etiquette toward God.
rows.anchor: şer‘an istiğfâra mev‘ud ve müterettib olan ahkâm, tevbe mânasında olan istiğfardadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can use ihtibak: ask pardon because God is Ghaffar, and repent because He is Tawwab, with one paired term omitted.
rows.anchor: Bir de bu âyette ihtibak sanatı olduğu söylenmiştir

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Âişe
rows.claim: Aisha reports that near the end of his life the Prophet often recited tasbih, praise, seeking forgiveness, and repentance; he said God had shown a sign in his community and ordered him to respond with these acts.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Âişe’den rivayet olunmuştur ki

rows.speaker: Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf says pairing tasbih with istighfar completes religion's pillars of obedience and protection from sin; for the infallible Prophet it also teaches humility, itself worship.
rows.anchor: Tefsîr-i Keşşâf’ta der ki: “Tesbih emriyle beraber istiğfar emri dinin kıvâmı olan emir ile emri tekmil içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound reports say the Prophet sought forgiveness one hundred times by day and by night.
rows.anchor: ‘ben gece ve gündüz yüz kere istiğfar ederim’

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi says worship remains deficient before God's majesty, so istighfar is prescribed after prayer, at dawn after night prayer, and after Hajj.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî der ki: “Âbid her ne kadar bezl-i mechud etse de Mâbud’un celâline lâyık olanı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports also prescribe istighfar after ablution and at a gathering's end; the Prophet used a closing supplication of tasbih, praise, forgiveness, and repentance.
rows.anchor: her meclisin hitâmında istiğfârın meşrû‘olduğu da rivayet olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This command signals the Prophet's approaching death; more commonly, it indicates that the religious mission was reaching completion.
rows.anchor: meşhuru da bu işaret, emr-i dinin tekâmülüyle davet vazifesinin tamama yaklaşmış olduğuna delâletten anlaşılmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised victory and mass entry fulfill the mission described in 61:9; with 40:77 and the names Tawwab and Maghfirat, the command signals the completed promise, the Prophet's return to God, and especially seeking forgiveness for his community.
rows.anchor: bu sûrede de nasr ve fethin geleceği ve halkın alay alay dîn-i hakka girmeye başladıklarını Resûlullah’ın muhakkak göreceği vaad olunarak

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: After the surah descended, the Prophet said God gave a servant the choice between this world and meeting Him, and the servant chose the meeting; Abu Bakr understood and offered their lives and families.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunmuştur ki, bu sûre nâzil olduğunda Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem bir hutbe îrad edip şöyle buyurmuştu

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Abbas
rows.claim: A report says the Companions rejoiced at the surah, but Abbas cried because he understood it to announce the Prophet's death; the Prophet confirmed him.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Abbas radıyallahu anh ağlamıştı

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi contrasts those who perceive God after seeing things with those who perceive Him before them; the latter path is more perfect because inference from cause to effect and root to branch is stronger.
rows.anchor: Râzî tefsirinde der ki: “Hak yolcularının seyrinde iki tarîk vardır; kimisi

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says the verse favors the superior path by placing two commands about the Creator before istighfar; majesty precedes beneficence and the final command recognizes human fault and divine generosity.
rows.anchor: Zira Hâlık ile iştigāli nefs ile iştigāle takdim ederek evvelâ Hâlık’a ait iki emr: tesbih ve hamd zikrolunmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descent toward people must lead back to God, not remain among creation; ending with Tawwab joins both paths in return to divine unity.
rows.anchor: halkta kalmak için değil, halktan Hâlık’a ekmel vechile rücû‘

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successful Prophet who received Kawthar saw conquests and crowds enter Islam as revelation matured; he faced worldly sovereignty and spoils alongside the afterlife reward of pure return to God.
rows.anchor: iki mükâfâtın tecellîsi karşısında bulunuyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Also called the Farewell Surah, it signals that the perfected religion's laws are entrusted to the community as the Prophet leaves bodily life and seeks God's meeting.
rows.anchor: Bir nâmı da Tevdî‘Sûresi olan bu sûre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph, after worldly success, asked to die as a Muslim and join the righteous; similarly, Muhammad chose meeting God over remaining in this world.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Yûsuf mülkte muvaffakıyetinin neticesinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Farewell Pilgrimage and sermon, the Prophet continued praising and glorifying God; the final revealed verse warned that all would return to Him and receive their deeds.
rows.anchor: “Bakınız tebliğ ettim mi? Bakınız tebliğ ettim mi?” diye diye îrad buyurduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During his final illness, the Prophet offered restitution for any harm, answered a claimant with three dirhams, and warned that worldly disgrace is easier than the hereafter's.
rows.anchor: üç dirhem iddia eden bir kişiye derhâl bedelini verdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed for Uhud's martyrs, repeated the report of a servant choosing God's meeting, recommended the Ansar, and Abu Bakr wept and pledged all he had.
rows.anchor: Sonra ashâb-ı Uhud’a dua etti ve onlar için istiğfar eyledi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In his final moments the Prophet prayed for help through death's agonies and uttered “the Highest Companion,” attaining the desired meeting with God.
rows.anchor: اَللّٰهُمَّ أَعِنيِّ عَلَي سَكَرَاتِ الْمَوْتِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad's death confirms he was a messenger like earlier messengers, as 3:144 says.
rows.anchor: وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌۭ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following Surat al-Lahab illustrates the fate of those who persist in disbelief and hostility; the Prophet's death cannot halt Islam's expansion.
rows.anchor: Peygamber’in vefatıyla İslâm’ın fütûhat ve intişârına halel gelmeyip ona düşmanlık edenlerin yine muradlarına eremeyecekleri anlatılmak üzere
